# Identity Hub Data Dictionary

**Dataset:** `bi-data-391216.identity_hub_data`
**Generated from:** [sql/identity_hub_ddl.sql](../sql/identity_hub_ddl.sql), [configs/identity_hub.yaml](../configs/identity_hub.yaml), [shared/identity_hub.py](../shared/identity_hub.py)

Every table in `identity_hub_data`: what it holds, every column with its type
and definition, and which connector produces the rows.

**How the hub is populated.** Connectors run in a fixed order (section 2). Each
one reads a source system, finds two identifiers that belong to the same person,
and emits an **edge** into `bn_id_hub` tagged with a `match_rule` and a
confidence. After every connector has run, union-find collapses the edge set into
connected components; each component becomes one `bn_id`, and the
identifier-to-`bn_id` mapping is published to `bn_id_xref`. Everything else in
the dataset is either an audit trail of that process or a debugging surface over
it.

**Where to start.** `bn_id_xref` is the consumer surface -- one row per
identifier, carrying the `bn_id` it resolved to. Join to it from any system that
knows an email, cookie or user id. `bn_id_neighbors` answers "why are these two
the same person". The rest is machinery.

## 2. How rows get made: connector run order

Each connector emits edges into `bn_id_hub`. They run in this order, and order matters -- later connectors can only merge clusters the earlier ones created.

|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Phase 0: localStorage/cookie co-occurrence | `connect_localstorage` | `LOCALSTORAGE_COOCCURRENCE` | -- |

## 3. Columns

### bn_id_persistence

event_type is 'MERGE' (rows written before 2026-07-30 said 'MERGED'; normalized by one-time backfill).

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `old_bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | Retired bn_id; PK of the redirect registry |
| `current_bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | Surviving bn_id this row redirects to |
| `event_type` | `STRING` |  | MERGE (redirects-only registry; no CREATE/SPLIT rows) |
| `event_date` | `DATE` |  | Date the row was written |
| `run_id` | `STRING` |  | Pipeline run that produced this row |
| `build_mode` | `STRING` |  | full \| incremental |
| `config_version` | `STRING` |  | identity_hub.yaml version that produced the row |
| `git_sha` | `STRING` |  | Commit the pipeline ran from; pairs with config_version for reproducibility |

**Special:**

- Redirect registry for retired ids. When two clusters merge, the losing `bn_id` gets a row here pointing at the survivor, so old references still resolve.
- **`event_type` is written as `MERGE`, and the registry holds redirects only.** For the full merge/split history query `bn_id_identity_changes` instead.

### bn_id_xref

One row per (identifier_type, identifier_value). identifier_key is the composite "{type}:{value}" and is unique. Used by every downstream join (profile_database, audience builders, debugging).

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier_key` | `STRING` | yes | "{identifier_type}:{identifier_value}" -- PK |
| `bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | Resolved person cluster ID. THE join key for profile_data and audiences |
| `identifier_type` | `STRING` | yes | bnfpvid \| client_id \| email \| mc_euid \| npi_number \| wp_user_id \| bionews_uk \| fbp \| phone \| ... (full list at the end of this file) |
| `identifier_value` | `STRING` | yes | The identifier itself. Emails are lowercased/trimmed; wp_user_id is site-qualified {site}:{id} |
| `cluster_tier` | `STRING` |  | tier1 (known) \| tier2 (anonymous) |
| `cluster_size` | `INT64` |  | Total identifiers in this bn_id cluster |
| `is_hcp` | `BOOL` |  | Cluster contains an NPI |
| `is_shared_workstation` | `BOOL` |  | >=2 mc_euids share this bnfpvid (flag only; edges removed at >=3) |
| `is_bot` | `BOOL` |  | Cluster matched bot heuristics; exclude from audience counts |
| `is_suspicious` | `BOOL` |  | cluster_health_score < 60 |
| `cluster_health_score` | `INT64` |  | 0-100 composite quality score |
| `last_seen` | `TIMESTAMP` |  | Most recent observation of this identifier anywhere in the graph |
| `source_profile` | `STRING` |  | Comma-separated source categories: browser, ga4, offline |

**Special:**

- `identifier_value` is normalised on write: emails lowercased and trimmed, `wp_user_id` site-qualified as `{site}:{id}` because WordPress reuses numeric ids across sites. Join on the normalised form or you will miss rows.
- `cluster_tier` is the single most important filter. `tier1` clusters contain a durable anchor (email, SSO key, NPI) and are real people; `tier2` clusters are cookie-only and are closer to browsers than humans.
- `is_bot`, `is_suspicious` and `is_shared_workstation` are advisory flags, not filters. Nothing removes those rows for you.

### bn_id_hub

One row per directional edge with confidence/source/match_rule. No natural single-column PK; queries filter by bn_id, identifier_*, or match_rule.

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | Cluster this edge ended up in AFTER union-find; not an input to the edge |
| `identifier_a_type` | `STRING` |  | Type of the first identifier in the pair |
| `identifier_a_value` | `STRING` |  | Value of the first identifier in the pair |
| `identifier_b_type` | `STRING` |  | Type of the second identifier in the pair |
| `identifier_b_value` | `STRING` |  | Value of the second identifier in the pair |
| `source_system` | `STRING` |  | acceptor \| bio_acceptor \| mailchimp \| ga4 \| npi_registry \| dmd_audiences \| wordpress \| aim_clickstream \| limesurvey \| gravity_forms |
| `link_type` | `STRING` |  | deterministic (observed on one row) \| probabilistic (inferred, e.g. IP+time) |
| `match_rule` | `STRING` |  | LOCALSTORAGE_COOCCURRENCE \| EMAIL_EXACT \| MC_EUID_BRIDGE \| UTM_CROSSWALK \| DEVICE_STAT_ID \| ... |
| `base_confidence` | `FLOAT64` |  | Confidence of a single observation, set by the connector config |
| `confidence` | `FLOAT64` |  | After log2 aggregation across repeated observations |
| `effective_confidence` | `FLOAT64` |  | confidence * decay_weight; only edges >= 0.80 stitch |
| `first_seen` | `TIMESTAMP` |  | Earliest observation of the link |
| `last_seen` | `TIMESTAMP` |  | Most recent observation of the link |
| `is_active` | `BOOL` |  | FALSE retires an edge without deleting it (this table is append-only) |
| `cluster_tier` | `STRING` |  | Tier of the cluster; denormalized for filtering |

**Special:**

- Append-only. Edges are retired by setting `is_active = FALSE`, never deleted, so an unfiltered `COUNT(*)` includes history.
- Three confidence columns, and they are not interchangeable. `base_confidence` is one observation, `confidence` aggregates repeated observations, and `effective_confidence` applies time decay. **Only edges with `effective_confidence >= 0.80` actually stitch.**
- `bn_id` is the cluster the edge ended up in *after* union-find. It is an output, not an input -- do not read it as 'the connector assigned this'.
- `first_seen` feeds `profile_core.source_created_at` for an allowlist of `match_rule` values. Rules not on that list are pipeline-stamped at build time and would silently corrupt acquisition dates.

### bn_id_neighbors

Cross-product of identifiers in the same bn_id cluster. The best surface for "why are these two linked?" debugging.

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | Cluster both nodes belong to |
| `node_type` | `STRING` |  | Type of the node being described |
| `node_value` | `STRING` |  | Value of the node being described |
| `neighbor_type` | `STRING` |  | Type of the co-clustered identifier |
| `neighbor_value` | `STRING` |  | Value of the co-clustered identifier |
| `confidence` | `FLOAT64` |  | Confidence of the edge that linked this pair |
| `match_rule` | `STRING` |  | Rule that linked the pair -- the answer to why are these two the same person |
| `source_system` | `STRING` |  | System the linking evidence came from |
| `first_seen` | `TIMESTAMP` |  | Earliest observation of the link |
| `last_seen` | `TIMESTAMP` |  | Most recent observation of the link |
| `cluster_tier` | `STRING` |  | Tier of the cluster; denormalized for filtering |

**Special:**

- The cross-product of identifiers inside each cluster, so it is the largest table in the dataset and grows quadratically with cluster size. Always filter by `bn_id`.
- `match_rule` here is the answer to 'why are these two linked' -- the fastest way to debug a suspicious merge.

### bn_id_identity_changes

MERGE = retired_bn_id collapsed into surviving_bn_id. SPLIT = a sub-cluster broke off from surviving_bn_id and got retired_bn_id as its new identity. Both surviving_bn_id and retired_bn_id are FKs to the persistence registry.

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_date` | `DATE` | yes | Date the merge or split was applied |
| `event_type` | `STRING` | yes | MERGE \| SPLIT |
| `surviving_bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | bn_id that continues to exist after the change |
| `retired_bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | bn_id retired (MERGE) or newly created for the split-off sub-cluster (SPLIT) |
| `node_count_moved` | `INT64` |  | How many identifiers changed cluster |
| `trigger_edge` | `STRING` |  | Identifier pair that caused the change, e.g. "email:foo@bar.com<->mc_euid:abc" |
| `run_id` | `STRING` | yes | Run that produced the snapshot; filter to bn_id_manifest.active_run_id |
| `build_mode` | `STRING` |  | full \| incremental |
| `config_version` | `STRING` |  | identity_hub.yaml version that produced the row |
| `git_sha` | `STRING` |  | Commit the pipeline ran from |

**Special:**

- The real merge/split audit trail. `SPLIT` means a sub-cluster broke off and took `retired_bn_id` as its new identity, so 'retired' does not always mean 'gone'.

### bn_id_node_index

Includes non-output nodes used for incremental rebuild targeting. (identifier_key, run_id) is the composite PK; queries usually filter to the latest run_id from bn_id_manifest.

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier_key` | `STRING` | yes | {identifier_type}:{identifier_value} |
| `bn_id` | `STRING` | yes | Cluster assigned in this run |
| `identifier_type` | `STRING` | yes | Type of the identifier |
| `is_output` | `BOOL` |  | TRUE if this node ended up in bn_id_xref |
| `cluster_tier` | `STRING` |  | Tier assigned in this run |
| `run_id` | `STRING` | yes | Run that produced the snapshot; filter to bn_id_manifest.active_run_id |

**Special:**

- One snapshot per run, including nodes that never reached `bn_id_xref`. **Filter to `bn_id_manifest.active_run_id`** or you will read several runs at once and multiply your counts.

### bn_id_metrics

One row per (run_id, metric_name). Tracks edge counts, component counts, and timing for every connector and pipeline phase.

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `STRING` | yes | Pipeline run the metric belongs to |
| `run_date` | `DATE` | yes | Date of the run |
| `metric_name` | `STRING` | yes | e.g. "localstorage.edges", "union_find.components" |
| `metric_value` | `FLOAT64` |  | Numeric value; counts and durations share this column |
| `build_mode` | `STRING` |  | full \| incremental |
| `config_version` | `STRING` |  | identity_hub.yaml version |
| `git_sha` | `STRING` |  | Commit the pipeline ran from |

**Special:**

- Long format: one row per (`run_id`, `metric_name`), values in a single `FLOAT64` column shared by counts and durations.

### bn_id_manifest

Tracks the last successfully promoted pipeline run. Downstream consumers should filter bn_id_metrics / bn_id_node_index by active_run_id.

| Column | Type | Req | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active_run_id` | `STRING` | yes | Run that downstream consumers should read |
| `promoted_at` | `TIMESTAMP` |  | When the run was promoted to active |
| `status` | `STRING` |  | active \| promoting \| failed |

**Special:**

- The pointer to the run downstream consumers should read. Anything that reads `bn_id_node_index` or `bn_id_metrics` should join here first.
